items.title: Dick Katz interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002
items.q: this little old lady named Janet Schenck who was the head of the school... So she says, I started to play my classical thing... she said, 'Oh that’s nice but it says here that you play jazz music. Would you play something for me?'

ctx.x: I just don’t know how he got in. Because I didn’t get in, I applied to Juilliard and I had to play a rigid classical repertoire, and they said well you play okay but this is for really serious classical advanced students and we have too many now so I was sort of discouraged. But I applied to Manhattan. This is interesting because I went in there and they had similar entrance requirements, this little old lady named Janet Schenck who was the head of the school, this classical maven and she was a wealthy social…
